purpose: Make the project a complete modern narrative adventure game built around the fixed film chronology rather than a sequence of film scenes.

canon_contract.fixed_story: Peter Jackson film chronology remains the mandatory spine.
canon_contract.side_content_rule: Optional play lives between fixed film anchors and may deepen place, character, skill and relationships but may not replace, skip, reorder or change required film outcomes.

order: Frodo is outside in Hobbiton rather than sharing the opening study scene with Bilbo
Frodo meets Gandalf on the Shire lane
Gandalf and Frodo travel through Hobbiton
Gandalf reaches Bag End and meets Bilbo
opening_truth.game_adaptation: Player control should begin in a film-safe Frodo free-play window around the Shire before/around the Gandalf lane encounter; optional tasks may exist there but the Gandalf/Bilbo/party anchors remain mandatory.

canon_contract.source_verification_rule: Every FILM_CORE scene must be verified against the available screenplay/film source before implementation. Do not rely on memory for scene order, character presence or mandatory outcomes when the source can be checked.
canon_contract.uncertainty_rule: If the exact film scene is not supported by the currently available source pack, mark it UNVERIFIED and do not invent the missing canonical detail. Original side content may still be designed only if it cannot conflict with the unresolved film beat.
priority_order: Character presence and knowledge at that exact point
Original game interaction inside safe gaps
Optional side content and systemic world activity

research_synthesis.adaptation: Place meaningful optional rewards off the critical path; discoveries should improve knowledge, utility, relationships or bounded character capabilities instead of generic stat inflation.
Use short local events discovered naturally in the world without filling the quest log with errands. The event should usually be solved where it is found.
Keep authored chapter hubs/regions semi-open rather than forcing a single corridor or attempting one giant seamless world.
Exploration, backtracking and side tasks trigger original companion conversation and relationship texture without changing canon.
Residents work, travel, gossip, react to danger and continue local routines so the player feels like part of a world rather than the only active object.
Reveal local map knowledge, landmarks and safe paths through actual traversal/discovery instead of showing every icon immediately.
Use route reading, mechanisms, runes, doors, bridges, sound/echo and terrain problems that fit Middle-earth rather than copying another game's supernatural puzzle grammar.

player_life_layer.goal: The character should feel alive beyond a health bar.

persistent_axes.role: sprint, climbing/traversal and bounded combat exertion
fear, Ring pressure and psychological strain
persistent_axes.rule: Presentation/context axis; never changes fixed canon outcomes.

persistent_axes.role: companion trust, banter and optional assistance
persistent_axes.rule: Unlocks content and reactions, not alternate film endings.
Lightweight utility inventory, not survival micromanagement.

benefits: spot tracks, clues and hidden discoveries more easily
clearer resistance feedback during fear/Ring-pressure gameplay without changing authored outcomes

quest_families.example: help a Shire resident prepare for the party or repair a fence
encounter a small local problem while traveling and resolve it immediately
walk, race, train, cook, grieve or prepare camp with a companion
read hoof marks, broken brush, tracks, old stone signs or enemy traces
find a safe crossing, hidden trail, ruined stair or alternate climb
open a forgotten passage, align a mechanism, interpret markings or follow echoes
gather firewood, herbs, food, rope, boats or weather shelter before moving on
avoid Riders, patrols or suspicious locals without mandatory combat
observe or help with Hobbit, Elven or Dwarven craft and customs
find a view, object, song, ruin or conversation that adds a meaningful Chronicle entry

side_play: Party Business: help residents move food, lanterns, benches and barrels before the celebration.
Sam's Garden: gather or identify flowers/herbs and repair a trampled garden edge.
Old Paths: discover shortcuts, mills, orchards and the riverbank to grow Wayfinding.
Hobbit Games: race, throwing/accuracy, hide-and-seek or simple festival contests before danger enters the story.
Local Gossip: listen to bounded resident conversations that seed Chronicle context without future knowledge.
Quiet Feet: optional stealth/traversal challenge through hedges and gardens that teaches crouch/awareness before the Black Rider sequence.
Stable Yard: help recover supplies or calm/manage travel gear.
Listen Before Asking: gather local clues through observation rather than quest-marker dialogue chains.
Inn Life: dice/table game or food-service micro-activity with no gambling economy.
Suspicious Footprints: small investigation that raises Perception but cannot reveal plot knowledge early.
Ranger Lessons: Strider teaches tracks, wind direction, concealment and camp placement.
Herb Search: find plausible healing/support plants before/after danger without replacing canonical healing events.
Safe Fire: choose a sheltered camp position and prepare supplies.
Ruins: read old markers and find non-story chambers or viewpoints.
Library/Maps: lore and route-study activity.
Smithy/Craft Observation: learn equipment/history without turning Rivendell into a loot shop.
Companion Conversations: optional original talks with future Fellowship members.
Valley Exploration: waterfalls, terraces, gardens and viewpoints with Chronicle rewards.
Training: bounded sparring, footwork, archery observation and movement challenges.
Camp Duties: firewood, cooking, watches and gear checks.
Snow Route Reading: choose safer short paths and shelter pockets during travel.
West Gate Study: inspect markings and nearby terrain without solving required story early.
Echo Navigation: use sound/landmarks to read side corridors.
Dwarven Reliefs: lore discoveries and environmental puzzles.
Lost Stores: optional supplies with risk, never required for story.
Quiet Passage: optional stealth route around lesser enemies before mandatory encounters.
Grief and Memory: companion moments that deepen Fellowship Bond.
Galadhrim Craft: observe rope, boats and local craft.
Forest Paths: quiet traversal and perception challenges.
River Preparation: optional supply/boat preparation before departure.
River Reading: currents, landing sites and shore signs.
Watch Rotation: short companion duty/memory moments.
Ruined Amon Hen: lore and route exploration before the fracture window closes.
Pursuit Signs: perception/stealth events that increase tension without preventing canonical attack.
Old Alliance Memory: inspect objects/places tied to earlier trust.
Tower Observation: learn the transformed valley through clues and views.
Escape Preparation: identify wind, height, guards and possible routes without changing the fixed escape outcome.

systemic_world_events.rule: Events are short, contextual, cheap, and chapter-aware. They never demand that the player abandon an urgent canonical scene.
examples: resident asks for quick local help
weather forces a brief shelter decision
companion notices tracks or a landmark
rare peaceful vista or wildlife moment
enemy scouting sign that can be observed or avoided
systemic_world_events.cooldowns: Use bounded cooldowns and per-region caps so the world feels alive rather than noisy.

accessibility_and_player_choice: Optional navigation hints can be enabled without changing story difficulty.
Story-focused difficulty should reduce combat pressure while preserving exploration and side content.
Side content should be skippable when the film story is urgent.
Conversation logs/Chronicle can preserve context for players returning after a break.
production_order: Finish Journey Discovery runtime and save proof.
Add Character Life axes as lightweight state, starting Stamina/Resolve/Supplies without survival grind.
Implement progression tracks as bounded utility/content unlocks.
Expand contextual side-play chapter by chapter using the quest families above.
Add Chronicle/menu presentation and map-knowledge reveal.
Add environmental puzzles/traversal and dynamic world events.
Validate each chapter for pacing so optional content never damages film urgency.

ensemble_viewpoint_rule.rule: Frodo is the central Ring-bearer, not the mandatory controller for every scene. When the film gives another character the meaningful action, that character may become the playable viewpoint.
